components.name: aesgcm
components.description: AES-128-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D, TLS 1.3's 12-byte nonce and 16-byte tag), sealed and opened in place, on AES and carry-less multiply instructions where the CPU has them and constant-time portable code elsewhere.

components.name: cpu
components.description: What the CPU has of the instructions the components use (AES, carry-less multiply, SHA-256, SHA-512, VAES), asked once for the process.

components.name: ecdsa
components.description: ECDSA signature verification on P-256 and P-384 (FIPS 186-4, SEC 1): strict DER signatures, uncompressed keys checked on the curve, Montgomery field arithmetic with P-256's special reduction and NAF double-scalar multiplies.

components.name: http1
components.description: HTTP/1.1 client side (RFC 9112) without I/O: requests written into a buffer, and an incremental response parser that takes any split of the input and hands body bytes back uncopied, for Content-Length, chunked and close-delimited bodies.

components.name: net
components.description: TCP over the system's sockets for a loop that serves many: a Listener and the Streams it accepts or that connect out, non-blocking, closed on exec or never inherited, no SIGPIPE; each owns its socket and its entry in a wait Set, which close removes before the socket is closed; errors by kind, IPv4 and IPv6.

components.name: resolve
components.description: Host lookup that never blocks the caller's loop, one API on Linux, macOS and Windows: start, poll, take the addresses, drop to cancel. The system answers: mDNSResponder through DNSServiceGetAddrInfo on macOS, on a socket the caller's poll waits on, sorted by RFC 6724 as getaddrinfo sorts; GetAddrInfoExW on Windows, asynchronous and cancellable, its callback signalling the caller's poll; the C library's getaddrinfo on Linux, on a thread of wait's, where a lookup cancelled after it started runs on to the system's timeout.

components.name: roots
components.description: Mozilla's trust anchors for TLS servers from NSS's certdata.txt at a release tag (MPL 2.0), with Mozilla's distrust-after dates, embedded as PEM and loaded into an x509::Store, with Mozilla's OneCRL revocations (intermediates and roots refused anywhere on a path); scripts/roots-gen.py rebuilds the file from a newer tag.

components.name: rsa
components.description: RSA signature verification (RFC 8017): RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 and RSASSA-PSS with MGF1 and a salt of the hash's length, SHA-256 or SHA-384, for moduli of 2048 to 4096 bits and exponents of at most 33 bits.

components.name: sha256
components.description: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4), HMAC-SHA256 (RFC 2104) and HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869), with SHA instructions where the CPU has them.

components.name: sha384
components.description: SHA-384 (FIPS 180-4), HMAC-SHA384 (RFC 2104) and HKDF-SHA384 (RFC 5869), with SHA512 instructions where the CPU has them.

components.name: tls
components.description: A TLS 1.3 client (RFC 8446) without I/O: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 with an X25519 key share, ECDSA and RSA-PSS server signatures, SNI, ALPN, HelloRetryRequest, KeyUpdate and close_notify; bytes in any split, application records opened in place in the receive buffer and sealed in place in the pending one.

components.name: trust
components.description: TLS server authentication by the operating system's trust, as Go's crypto/x509 does it: macOS's SecTrustEvaluateWithError and Windows's CertGetCertificateChain with the SSL policy, on a thread a poll loop waits on, and on Linux x509::verify against the system's anchors (its bundle and certificate directories, or SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR, read through the C library). system() also loads the anchors themselves on all three: macOS's trust domains with their SSL trust settings, Windows's ROOT store less what is disabled for server authentication or Disallowed.

components.name: wait
components.description: What a program's loop waits on, for every component that works while it runs: a Set of any number of descriptors (sockets on Windows), each with its interest and a key, and deadlines on the monotonic clock, level-triggered on epoll (Linux), kqueue (macOS), socket notifications (Windows 11, Server 2022) or WSAPoll (earlier Windows), and a Waker for other threads; a component's Wait (up to two descriptors and a timeout), which a Set follows or block waits on alone; and a pool of at most 32 threads with a cancellable FIFO line, and the close-on-exec pipe (Linux and macOS) or non-inherited loopback socket pair (Windows) that says the work is done.

components.name: x25519
components.description: X25519 key agreement (RFC 7748): a constant-time Montgomery ladder over five 51-bit limbs.

components.name: x509
components.description: X.509 (RFC 5280) for TLS server authentication without I/O: a strict DER parser that borrows the certificate, a store of trust anchors from PEM or DER, and chain verification for a host at a given time, with paths built through intermediates in any order, name constraints as Go enforces them, bounded depth and signature checks, and the leaf's key for TLS 1.3's CertificateVerify.
